info.name: TurbulenceFX
info.comment: A filter effect that utilises the Perlin turbulence function.

description.p: This filter effect creates an image using the Perlin turbulence function. It allows the synthesis of artificial textures like clouds or marble. For a detailed description the of the Perlin turbulence function, see "Texturing and Modeling", Ebert et al, AP Professional, 1994. The resulting image will fill the entire filter primitive subregion for this filter primitive.
It is possible to create bandwidth-limited noise by synthesizing only one octave.

The effect implements the SVG feTurbulence primitive. Kōtuku extends it with control over the octave stack (Persistence, Lacunarity and Normalise), the mapping of the result (Amplitude and Offset), the noise domain (OriginX, OriginY and Angle), seamless repetition (PeriodX and PeriodY), animation (Phase and PhasePeriod), colour ramps (ColourMap and Stops) and two further Type functions, BILLOW and RIDGED. Each extension field defaults to the value that reproduces SVG output exactly. The Compliance field declares whether the extensions are permitted.

The following order is used for applying the pseudo random numbers. An initial seed value is computed based on Seed. Then the implementation computes the lattice points for R, then continues getting additional pseudo random numbers relative to the last generated pseudo random number and computes the lattice points for G, and so on for B and A.

action.name: Draw
action.comment: Render the effect to the target bitmap.
action.prototype: ERR acDraw(*Object, DOUBLE X, DOUBLE Y, DOUBLE Width, DOUBLE Height)

input.param: The X position of the region to be drawn.
The Y position of the region to be drawn.
The width of the region to be drawn.
The height of the region to be drawn.

description.p: Draw fails with ERR::InvalidValue if an extension field is in use while the resolved Compliance is SVG1 or SVG2, if Stitch is combined with PeriodX or PeriodY, if Stitch or a period is combined with an Angle that is not a multiple of 360, or if Stitch, a period or PhasePeriod is combined with several octaves and a fractional Lacunarity. A warning is logged in each case. It fails with ERR::OutOfRange if the drawn area or Phase lies so far from the origin, at the finest octave, that lattice coordinates can no longer be represented, or if a period of the finest octave cannot be represented.

field.name: Amplitude
field.comment: Scales the mapped noise value.

description.p: The noise value is mapped to the range [0, 1] as described for Type, multiplied by Amplitude and then added to Offset. The result is clamped to [0, 1] for output. The value must be finite and defaults to 1. This is a Kōtuku extension; see Compliance.

field.name: Angle
field.comment: Rotates the noise domain clockwise about its origin, in degrees.

description.p: The rotation is applied about the point given by OriginX and OriginY. The value must be finite and defaults to 0. A stitched or periodic domain cannot be rotated: if Stitch, PeriodX or PeriodY is set, the Angle must be a multiple of 360 or the effect will fail to draw.

If VectorFilter.PrimitiveUnits is BOUNDING_BOX, the rotation applies in bounding-box units and therefore appears skewed for a bounding box that is not square. This is a Kōtuku extension; see Compliance.

field.name: ColourMap
field.comment: Draws IMAGE output through a pre-defined colour ramp.

description.p: The noise value of each sample is computed from the alpha lattice, as for HEIGHT output, and clamped to [0, 1]. It then selects a colour from the named colourmap, from the first colour at 0 to the last at 1. The following colourmaps from the matplotlib and seaborn projects are supported: cmap:crest, cmap:flare, cmap:icefire, cmap:inferno, cmap:magma, cmap:mako, cmap:plasma, cmap:rocket, cmap:viridis.

Setting a colourmap replaces custom Stops. Set an empty string to clear the ramp and restore the four independent noise channels. Ramp colours are drawn as authored in either colour space. HEIGHT output ignores the ramp. Unknown names fail with ERR::NotFound. This is a Kōtuku extension; see Compliance.

field.name: Compliance
field.comment: Declares whether SVG restrictions apply to the effect.

description.p: The default, INHERIT, uses the VectorScene.Compliance of the scene that owns the filter, or NONE if there is no scene. An explicit value always overrides the scene.

The extension fields are Persistence, Lacunarity, Normalise, Amplitude, Offset, OriginX, OriginY, Angle, PeriodX, PeriodY, Phase, PhasePeriod, ColourMap, Stops and the BILLOW and RIDGED values of Type. When the compliance is SVG1 or SVG2, each extension field must remain at its default:

list.li: Initialisation fails with ERR::InvalidValue if the compliance is set explicitly and an extension field is in use.
After initialisation, writing a value other than the default to an extension field returns ERR::NoSupport. Writing the default is always permitted.
Setting SVG1 or SVG2 after initialisation returns ERR::InvalidState while an extension field is in use.
If the compliance is inherited from an SVG scene and an extension field is in use, Draw logs a warning and fails with ERR::InvalidValue.

description.p: SVG1 and SVG2 currently apply the same restrictions.

field.name: FX
field.comment: The base frequency for noise on the X axis.

description.p: The frequency must be finite and non-negative. The default value is zero.

field.name: FY
field.comment: The base frequency for noise on the Y axis.

description.p: The frequency must be finite and non-negative. The default value is zero.

field.name: Lacunarity
field.comment: The frequency multiplier between octaves.

description.p: Each octave samples the noise Lacunarity times more finely than the previous one. The value must lie in the range [1, 8] and defaults to 2, the fixed multiplier of SVG. If Stitch is enabled and there is more than one octave, the value must be an integer, otherwise Draw fails with ERR::InvalidValue. The same applies if PeriodX or PeriodY is set. This is a Kōtuku extension; see Compliance.

field.name: Normalise
field.comment: Divides the octave sum by its total weight.

description.p: If TRUE, the sum of the octaves is divided by the sum of their weights, Persistence^0 + ... + Persistence^(Octaves-1), before it is mapped. This keeps several octaves within the range of a single octave, so that changing Octaves or Persistence does not change the overall contrast. Defaults to FALSE. This is a Kōtuku extension; see Compliance.

field.name: Octaves
field.comment: The numOctaves parameter for the noise function.

description.p: Defaults to 1. Runtime writes accept values from 0 to 30.

field.name: Offset
field.comment: Adds to the scaled noise value.

description.p: See Amplitude. The value must be finite and defaults to 0. This is a Kōtuku extension; see Compliance.

field.name: OriginX
field.comment: The horizontal origin of the noise domain.

description.p: The noise is sampled relative to this point, so moving the origin translates the noise without changing it. Angle rotates the domain about the origin, and PeriodX and PeriodY measure their repeats from it.

The origin is expressed in primitive units and is measured from primitive-unit (0, 0), which is also the origin of SVG feTurbulence. A percentage refers to the width of the filter region. The value must be finite and defaults to 0. This is a Kōtuku extension; see Compliance.

field.name: OriginY
field.comment: The vertical origin of the noise domain.

description.p: A percentage refers to the height of the filter region. The value must be finite and defaults to 0. See OriginX. This is a Kōtuku extension; see Compliance.

field.name: OutputMode
field.comment: Selects an image or a linear height result from the noise's alpha channel.

description.p: Use HEIGHT when passing the result to enhanced LightingFX or height-output BlurFX. HEIGHT output ignores ColourMap and Stops.

field.name: PeriodX
field.comment: Repeats the noise horizontally after this number of lattice cells.

description.p: The first octave repeats exactly every PeriodX / FX primitive units, measured from OriginX, and octave k repeats every PeriodX * Lacunarity^k cells of its own lattice, so the full octave stack repeats with no seam. Unlike Stitch, the period does not adjust the frequency or depend on the primitive subregion.

The value must lie in the range [0, 1048576], and 0, the default, disables horizontal repetition. A period cannot be combined with Stitch or a rotated domain, and a period with several octaves requires an integer Lacunarity; Draw fails with ERR::InvalidValue otherwise. This is a Kōtuku extension; see Compliance.

field.name: PeriodY
field.comment: Repeats the noise vertically after this number of lattice cells.

description.p: The value must lie in the range [0, 1048576], and 0, the default, disables vertical repetition. See PeriodX. This is a Kōtuku extension; see Compliance.

field.name: Persistence
field.comment: The weight of each octave relative to the previous one.

description.p: Octave k is weighted by Persistence^k. The value must lie in the range [0, 1] and defaults to 0.5, the fixed weight of SVG. Lower values give smoother results, and a value of 0 leaves the first octave only. This is a Kōtuku extension; see Compliance.

field.name: Phase
field.comment: Animates the noise by moving through a third lattice dimension.

description.p: The noise is a slice of 3-D gradient noise, and Phase selects the position of the slice in lattice cells. Changing it gradually makes the pattern evolve smoothly, and a change of about one cell gives an unrelated pattern. Octave k moves Lacunarity^k times faster, so fine detail changes faster than coarse detail.

A Phase of 0, the default, reproduces the noise exactly as drawn without animation. Other values cost about twice as much to draw. The noise does not repeat unless PhasePeriod is set. The value must be finite. This is a Kōtuku extension; see Compliance.

field.name: PhasePeriod
field.comment: Loops the Phase animation after this number of lattice cells.

description.p: If set, the noise at Phase + PhasePeriod is identical to the noise at Phase, so an animation that advances Phase from 0 to PhasePeriod loops without a seam. Octave k repeats after PhasePeriod * Lacunarity^k cells of its own lattice. Small periods give short loops with less variety: a period of 1 returns to its starting pattern after a single cell.

The value must lie in the range [0, 1048576], and 0, the default, disables looping. A period with several octaves requires an integer Lacunarity; Draw fails with ERR::InvalidValue otherwise. This is a Kōtuku extension; see Compliance.

field.name: Seed
field.comment: The starting number for the pseudo random number generator.

description.p: If the value is undefined, the effect is as if a value of 0 were specified. When the seed number is handed over to the algorithm it must first be truncated, i.e. rounded to the closest integer value towards zero. Changing Seed rebuilds the noise lattice and invalidates the cached result.

field.name: Stitch
field.comment: If TRUE, stitching will be enabled at the tile's edges.

description.p: By default, the turbulence algorithm will sometimes show discontinuities at the tile borders. If Stitch is set to TRUE then the algorithm will automatically adjust base frequency values such that the node's width and height (i.e., the width and height of the current subregion) contains an integral number of the Perlin tile width and height for the first octave.

The baseFrequency will be adjusted up or down depending on which way has the smallest relative (not absolute) change as follows: Given the frequency, calculate lowFreq = floor(width*frequency) / width and hiFreq = ceil(width * frequency) / width. If frequency/lowFreq < hiFreq/frequency then use lowFreq, else use hiFreq. While generating turbulence values, generate lattice vectors as normal for Perlin Noise, except for those lattice points that lie on the right or bottom edges of the active area (the size of the resulting tile). In those cases, copy the lattice vector from the opposite edge of the active area.

field.name: Stops
field.comment: Draws IMAGE output through a custom colour ramp.

description.p: The noise value of each sample is computed from the alpha lattice, as for HEIGHT output, and clamped to [0, 1]. It then selects a colour from the gradient defined by the stops, including the opacity of each stop. At least two stops are required, or the setter fails with ERR::InvalidValue. A ramp from opaque black to opaque white draws the noise as greyscale.

Setting stops replaces any named ColourMap. Set an empty array to clear the ramp and restore the four independent noise channels. Ramp colours are drawn as authored in either colour space. HEIGHT output ignores the ramp. This is a Kōtuku extension; see Compliance.

field.name: Type
field.comment: Selects the function that combines the octaves of noise.

description.p: Each octave k samples gradient noise n at Lacunarity^k times the base frequency and weights it by Persistence^k. The weighted terms are summed and the sum is mapped to the range [0, 1]:

types.type: The term is abs(n) and the sum is used directly. This is the default.
The term is n and the sum s is mapped to (s + 1) / 2.
The term is 2 * sqrt(2) * abs(n) - 1 and the sum s is mapped to (s + 1) / 2. The rounded lobes resemble cumulus cloud.
The term is (1 - sqrt(2) * abs(n))^2, multiplied by twice the previous octave's term clamped to [0, 1]. The sum is used directly. The sharp crests resemble mountain ridges or veins.

description.p: BILLOW and RIDGED are Kōtuku extensions that are not available under SVG Compliance.

field.name: XMLDef
field.comment: Describes the primitive using the FilterEffect.XMLDef format.

description.p: The element that is written depends on the resolved Compliance. If the compliance resolves to SVG1 or SVG2, the primitive is written as a standard feTurbulence element. If Compliance is explicitly NONE, it is always written as xvg:feFractalNoise, so that the declaration survives a round trip. If Compliance is INHERIT and resolves to NONE, feTurbulence is written when every extension field is at its default, and xvg:feFractalNoise otherwise.
In each case, HEIGHT output is described by an xvg:outputMode attribute. The xvg:feFractalNoise element only includes attributes whose fields differ from their defaults.

constants.comment: Output modes for ImageFX, TurbulenceFX, BlurFX, WaveFunctionFX and CellularFX.
constants.const: Produce a linear floating-point scalar surface for numerical filter inputs.
Produce the usual RGBA image. This is the default.
BlurFX preserves its input format, including scalar and vector floats.
Use the Compliance of the scene that owns the filter, or NONE if there is no scene.
Kotuku extensions to the standard are permitted.
Sum rescaled absolute noise, giving rounded, cloud-like lobes.
Use a ridged multifractal, giving sharp crests.

struct.name: GradientStop
struct.comment: Describes a colour stop for the Gradient Stops field.
struct.field: An offset in the range of 0 - 1.0
